problem_statement: ND (Neighbor Discovery) packet validation on input is incorrect for Router Advertisements, Neighbor Solicitations, and Neighbor Advertisements. When an incoming ND packet has an invalid hop limit (not 255), an invalid length, or an invalid multicast address, the packet should be dropped. However, the current logic only drops the packet if the ICMPv6 code field is non-zero, which is never the case for valid ND packets. This means malformed ND packets with wrong hop limits or lengths are silently accepted instead of being dropped.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/ipv6 -s tests/net/ipv6/net.ipv6 -s net.ipv6 -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The problem statement clearly describes the bug (validation gated on icmp_hdr->code != 0) and the expected behaviour (drop on invalid hop limit, length, or multicast address independently), covering all three handlers (RA, NS, NA). The hidden tests verify the fix using pre-existing infrastructure (net_stats_ipv6_nd, NET_REQUEST_STATS_GET_IPV6_ND, CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS) that the agent does not need to invent; the agent only needs to change the validation logic so that bad packets are dropped, which the tests confirm via the drop counter.
